content.comment_body: Does anyone know the limit for [product_name] Ethernet/IP port? For example, is there a restriction on how many [product_name] units and other devices can be connected in the same Ethernet segment? If the ARP table of [product_name] is 16 entries long, it means less than 16 IP devices should be connected for stable operation. Thank you for any advice.

Hello, If I understand you correctly, you’re referring to network classes. This is not specific to [product_name]. The number of devices you can connect to an Ethernet segment depends on the network class configuration. For instance, with an IP address like 192.168.0.x (which is a Class C network), up to 255 devices can be connected. For more details, refer to Wikipedia on network classes. Hope this helps.

Sorry, but that's not correct. If you connect and use more devices than can fit within the length of the ARP table, then one or more devices will not be listed in the table. This can cause excessive ARP traffic on the network segment and may result in communication timeouts, since every packet would require a new ARP query.
